diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber ONU is offline and deregistered from the PON (MPCP DEREG), causing a complete loss of service. The exact local cause is not proven, but it is most likely an ONU power/device fault or a customer-side drop/connector issue.
evidence: The target ONU is explicitly offline in CRM and live probing, with auth_flag 'Unauth' and exchange state 'MPCP DEREG'.
Live readings are null because the ONU is not online; zero/null optical values are no-reading indicators, not strong-signal readings.
All six observed peer ONUs on EPON0/4 are online with normal RX power around -20 to -22 dBm and normal TX power around +2.3 to +2.4 dBm, so the PON port and splitter path are not broadly failing.

The subscriber's seven-day optical history was stable: RX remained approximately -21 to -22 dBm, TX remained within the normal range, distance stayed constant at 133, and TX bias remained healthy around 11 mA.
The OLT responds normally and its CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are healthy; the all-PON failure result is therefore a false diagnostic/probe critical condition rather than an OLT failure.
The router heartbeat is healthy, VLAN 1094 is present and matches the expected customer VLAN, and RADIUS data is consistent, ruling out router, VLAN, and authentication database faults.
The subscriber's last disconnect was at 16:09, matching the complaint timing, while traffic dropped sharply on the latest day, confirming customer-specific service loss.
The issue affects only the target ONU; the other customers on the same PON port remain online.

remediation.action: Contact the customer to verify power and cabling, then power-cycle the ONU. If it does not re-register, inspect and clean the customer drop and optical connectors, test the fibre, and replace the ONU if necessary. Do not alter the OLT, PON port, VLAN, or RADIUS configuration.

ground_truth.root_cause: This customer's ONU has genuinely deregistered, with a clean signal history up to the cut-off. The OLT's concurrent critical health alarm is a separate false positive: the live probe answers normally for every other ONU on the port, so the health check result does not reflect the device state.
expected_reasoning: The customer's ONU returns responds true with online 0, a definite offline answer
Signal history was flat and healthy until the cut-off four hours ago, so power loss or ONU failure is indicated
The OLT health record separately reports critical with all PONs failed
However the live probe answers normally for every other ONU on EPON0/4, returning real RX and TX values
OLT ping and SNMP both succeed, uptime is 44 days, and CPU, memory and temperature are at baseline
If the OLT or its PON ports had genuinely failed, no ONU would be responding and many more customers would be offline
CRM shows the OLT's offline count consistent with the normal background rate, not a mass outage
The health alarm is therefore a false critical and must not be conflated with this customer's real fault
Two findings coexist: one genuine single-customer outage and one monitoring defect

expected_escalation.review_reason: A concurrent false critical health alarm on this OLT should be raised separately with monitoring

distractors: The critical OLT alarm invites attributing the customer outage to an OLT failure
Dismissing the alarm too readily risks also dismissing the genuine customer fault
Only one customer is affected despite an alarm claiming the whole OLT
